definition: In Greek antiquity, a band or company assembled in honor of a divinity; especially, a Dionysiac band or procession in which men and women took part in character, with boisterous mirth and music, and bearing attributes of the god; sometimes a political, commercial, social, or benevolent association or guild; specifically, the mythological band of nymphs, maenads, satyrs, etc., forming the personal cortège of Dionysus, and often represented in sculpture and painting.
